content.chapter: Chapter 1 — A Green Plan for Europe
objectives: Say what the green deal wants.
Use “want to” with a verb.
Say how people repair, reuse, and recycle.
content.pedagogy: Start from something learners can see or touch. Listen first with one question, then read and do one concrete task: Find three dates or numbers: 11 December 2019, 2050, zero. Grammar grows out of the chapter’s own sentences.
priorKnowledge: Everyday words for home and school.
anticipatedMisconceptions: The European Commission is part of the EU; it is not a country.
content.grammarFocus:
Targets: Wants to + Verb, Repair, Reuse, Recycle, My Green Plan.
Notice (Activity 1): “The Green Deal wants to protect our world.” What comes after “wants to”?
Build (Activity 2): What do people do in a circular economy?
Use (Activity 3): What do you want to do for a cleaner world?
beforeReading: Show a recycling bin and a broken toy. Ask: “Throw it away or repair it?”
duringReading: First listening: When did the EU share the Green Deal?
Find three dates or numbers: 11 December 2019, 2050, zero.
afterReading: Language Focus: Wants to + Verb (Activity 1), Repair, Reuse, Recycle (Activity 2), My Green Plan (Activity 3).
content.lessonPlan: 0–5 Hook; 5–12 Listen with books closed, then read along; 12–19 Find three dates or numbers: 11 December 2019, 2050, zero. 19–23 Quick Challenge; 23–31 Language Focus Activities 1–2; 31–38 Activity 3 in pairs; 38–40 Exit ticket.
discussionPoints: What can we repair at home instead of throwing it away?
What does the EU want by 2050?
interactiveTips: Use the “Shared in 2019” hotspot when you check the answer.
Use the “Repair and Reuse” hotspot when you check the answer.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Give the Word Notes (protect, economy, greenhouse gas, emissions, eco-friendly, circular economy, recycle, rule) on cards before reading. Let learners copy the model sentence from Activity 3 first.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Tell your partner three sentences about a green plan for your home. Add one more sentence of your own.

formativeAssessment: I can say what the Green Deal wants.
I can use “want to” with a verb.
I can say how people repair, reuse, and recycle.
expectedResponses: I want to use less water. I want to repair my old bag. I want to recycle paper at school.
content.transferTask: Tell your partner three sentences about a green plan for your home.
content.teacherReflection: Did learners find the answer in the text, or did they guess?

exitTicket: Answer in one sentence: What does the EU want by 2050?

content.chapter: Chapter 3 — Why Is the Green Deal Important?
objectives: Say why fossil fuels are a problem.
Use “too much”, “because of”, and “so”.
Talk about energy at home.
content.pedagogy: Start from something learners can see or touch. Listen first with one question, then read and do one concrete task: Underline the reasons with “because of” and the results with “so”. Grammar grows out of the chapter’s own sentences.
priorKnowledge: Everyday words for home and school.
anticipatedMisconceptions: Energy is a problem today for two reasons: pollution and high prices.

Targets: Too Much, Because Of, So, Too Much at Home.

Use (Activity 3): Where do people use too much?

duringReading: First listening: Which of these is a fossil fuel?
Underline the reasons with “because of” and the results with “so”.
afterReading: Language Focus: Too Much (Activity 1), Because Of, So (Activity 2), Too Much at Home (Activity 3).
content.lessonPlan: 0–5 Hook; 5–12 Listen with books closed, then read along; 12–19 Underline the reasons with “because of” and the results with “so”. 19–23 Quick Challenge; 23–31 Language Focus Activities 1–2; 31–38 Activity 3 in pairs; 38–40 Exit ticket.

interactiveTips: Use the “Fossil Fuels” hotspot when you check the answer.
Use the “Expensive Energy” hotspot when you check the answer.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Give the Word Notes (pollution, coal, fossil fuels, net-zero) on cards before reading. Let learners copy the model sentence from Activity 3 first.

formativeAssessment: I can say why fossil fuels are a problem.

content.chapter: Chapter 4 — Energy from the Wind and the Sun
objectives: Say why countries use wind and sun energy.
Compare with -er: cheaper, faster.

content.grammarFocus:
Targets: Cheaper, Faster, Compare Energy, Compare Two Ways.
Notice (Activity 1): “It is often cheaper.” “The green change must be faster.” What does -er do?

beforeReading: Show a photo of wind turbines. Ask: “What do they make?”

formativeAssessment: I can say why countries use wind and sun energy.

objectives: Say what an energy label shows.

metadata.title: The European Green Deal A2 — Teacher’s Book
metadata.subtitle: First draft for review: chapter-by-chapter support and 40-minute lesson plans
metadata.estimatedDuration: 8 chapter units of 40 minutes each. Whole-book review pages follow separately.
metadata.targetLearners: Learners who can follow short supported informational texts and give short spoken or written answers with frames.
metadata.purpose: Develop A2 listening, reading, speaking and writing through a short informational text about the European Green Deal, its goals, and what it means for everyday life and work.
metadata.approachDesc: Every chapter follows the same route: listen and read for meaning, check with the Quick Challenge, then Look → Practise → Use in the Language Focus, with grammar taken from the chapter’s own sentences.
metadata.assessmentEvidence: Eight Quick Challenges, Language Focus tasks, exit tickets, Knowledge Check, Vocabulary Challenge, Language Review and Final Challenge.

formative: Short spoken and written Use tasks

readingFramework.before: A short start from something learners can see: a picture, an object or a date.
readingFramework.during: Listen first with one question, then read and do one concrete task.
readingFramework.after: Quick Challenge, then the Language Focus, then a short Use task about the learners’ own life.

vocabularyApproach.selection: The Word Notes of each chapter.
vocabularyApproach.method: Meet the word in the chapter, check its note, use it in a sentence.
vocabularyApproach.recycling: Key Terms, Master Glossary and Vocabulary Challenge.

metadata.grammarApproach: Inductive: learners notice a form in a real sentence, practise it, then use it about their own life.

skillsFocus.reading: Find facts and numbers in an informational text.
skillsFocus.listening: Listen for one key fact first.
skillsFocus.speaking: Short pair talk about home, school and town.

metadata.differentiationNotes: Word Notes on cards before reading; model sentences to copy; extra sentence for fast finishers.

sensitiveNotes.title: Notes for the teacher
notes: The text is about EU policy. Türkiye’s own plan (2021, net zero by 2053) is in Chapter 8.
